rationale: Block 3 establishes the diagnostic pivot between inflammatory and degenerative arthritis; this interaction tests whether students understand the key temporal feature (morning stiffness duration) that differentiates the two.
Block 6 covers RA pathogenesis and serology; anti-CCP specificity versus sensitivity is a classic examination trap that tests depth of understanding beyond basic recall.

Block 11 covers AS clinical examination and diagnostic criteria including HLA-B27 and the bamboo spine radiological sign; this question tests the ability to link the radiological finding to its pathological basis.

Block 14 covers the management hierarchy — NSAIDs symptom relief, DMARDs disease modification, biologics for refractory cases — and methotrexate as the anchor first-line DMARD for RA; a critical prescribing knowledge trap.
